claims.statement: The five store roots are spelled out in exactly one place, `defaultSessionRoots(home = os.homedir())` in scanners/index.ts, resolved once when `SessionsService` is constructed (`options.roots ?? defaultSessionRoots()`) and injected through `collectSessions(roots, now)` into one scanner per tool key; no scanner resolves a user path itself, and the only caller drives a 1 Hz sampling round (`DEFAULT_TICK_MS = 1000`, a kernel timer that either calls `bridge.tick()` in the in-process assembly or `sessions.refresh()` directly in the data-plane utility process), so every store is re-read at most about once per second regardless of how often the renderer asks.

Every SQLite store is opened through the single helper `openReadOnly`, which constructs `DatabaseSync` with `{ readOnly: true }` — the node:sqlite equivalent of the Python era's `file:…?mode=ro` URI that ADR-0003 names — and then sets `PRAGMA busy_timeout = 500`, closing the handle and rethrowing if that pragma fails; the read-only open makes it impossible for the panel to write to a tool's database, and the 500 ms timeout makes a database held exclusively by its own writer fail fast into the skip-with-log path instead of stalling the 1 Hz round. Only the hermes and zcode scanners open SQLite.

The qoder store is a JSONL append log at `<root>/projects/<project dir>/<session id>.jsonl` whose file mtime supplies the age, plus `<root>/tasks/<session id>/*.json` files; `sessionLast` reads at most the last 131072 bytes to classify the newest assistant/user record, `projectName` at most the last 65536 bytes for the newest `cwd` with a fallback to the jsonl's parent directory name, and `taskStats` counts only the task files that parse as JSON, counting `status == "completed"` as done and returning the first `in_progress` subject as `current` (which currently has no consumer). Because the log is read only from its end, a growing or partly corrupt file still yields a session with a degraded state.

The hermes store is a SQLite `state.db` whose `sessions` table is queried only for `id, cwd, last_activity_at, started_at, end_reason, archived` (title and ended_at exist upstream, as the fixture schema shows, but are never selected), plus a separate lease file at `<root>/runtime/active_sessions.json` shaped `{"entries": [{"lease_id", "session_id", "pid", "updated_at"}]}` from which only `session_id` is used; the lease read happens before the database is opened and has its own try/catch returning an empty set, so a broken lease file degrades to "no leases" while the tool still scans.

hermes derives liveness from a cross-check that makes it the strongest signal tier: activity is `last_activity_at` falling back to `started_at`, a row where both are null is dropped and a value that is neither null nor a number throws and skips the whole tool; `running` is true when the session id appears in the active lease set or when `end_reason` is null and age is within 90 s; the state is RUN for a running session, DONE whenever an end reason is set even if the session was touched seconds ago, and IDLE only for an unended quiet session; archived rows and rows older than 600 s never enter the list, and the store exposes no task progress (tasks_done/tasks_total stay null).

The zcode store is a SQLite database at `<root>/cli/db/db.sqlite` with a `session` table (id, directory, title, time_created, time_updated, time_archived) and a `todo` table (session_id, content, status, position) — the same DDL the fixture builds; the scanner ages rows as `now - time_updated / 1000` from that millisecond column and gets progress from one grouped query, `SUM(status = 'completed')` over `COUNT(*)` keyed by session_id, so a session with no todos reports `(0, 0)` — a real "no tasks yet" rather than the null used by tools with no progress concept — while `SUM` over an all-null status group yields a null done count with a positive total.

zcode applies three filters inside the scanner before a row becomes a session: rows with a non-null `time_archived`, rows with a null `time_updated` that cannot be aged, and ids carrying the constant `ZCODE_SUBAGENT_PREFIX = 'sess_subagent_'` are dropped, the last because real subagent rows swamped the list at acceptance time; that prefix is a convention extracted from observed data rather than a published upstream concept, and the filters never reach the seam.

The kimi code store is a per-session directory tree `<root>/sessions/<workspace>/<session>/state.json` plus `agents/main/wire.jsonl`; `state.json` is the mandatory file and its `workDir` key supplies the project as the last path segment (empty when the key is absent), while liveness comes from the newer of the two file mtimes rather than from the `updatedAt` field inside `state.json`, and a `wire.jsonl` that does not exist is simply left out of that comparison.

kimi code degrades per session rather than per tool: an unreadable or unparseable `state.json` skips only that session while sibling sessions of the same tool still appear, a missing `sessions/` directory yields an empty list, but a `state.json` that parses into a non-object throws and costs the whole tool; only the migrated `~/.kimi-code` tree is read (the legacy `.kimi` directory is deliberately out of scope), and because the tail of `wire.jsonl` carries config/mcp events with no user/assistant role signal, every non-RUN kimi code session lands on DONE exactly like zcode and CONFIRM is unreachable.

The kimi work store is two flat JSON maps in the kimi-desktop agent directory — `conversation-statuses.json` (key to status string, and the iteration source of the scanner) and `conversation-context-usage.json` (key to an entry carrying contextUsage and an ISO-8601 `updatedAt`) — keyed by composite conversation identifiers of the form `agent:main:main:conversation:<uuid>`, of which only the last colon-separated segment is kept as the session id; a conversation is listed only when it has an entry in both maps with a non-empty string `updatedAt`, and either file failing to parse skips the whole tool.

kimi work is the accepted title-less degradation case: its row carries an empty project string and null task progress because the conversation bodies live in the tool's own private store, so parsing them was rejected in ADR-0003; age comes from the per-conversation `updatedAt` and not from a file mtime, so one fresh conversation cannot promote older ones to RUN; and the state is RUN within 90 s, DONE only for the observed status value "completed", and IDLE for any unrecognised status value.

Failure isolation and degradation are enforced at the seam: a root whose key is absent from `SCANNERS` is skipped with no log line at all, so a typo in a roots mapping silently drops a tool, while a scanner that raises is caught per tool, prints one `console.warn` line naming the tool, and leaves the other four tools scanning, so an upstream format change surfaces as a quietly missing tool rather than a broken panel; a round that fails as a whole makes `SessionsService` store an empty list rather than stale rows.

Task progress is a per-store capability, not a universal field: `tasks_done`/`tasks_total` are numeric only for qoder (from `tasks/<session id>/*.json`) and zcode (from the `todo` table aggregation), and stay null for hermes, kimi code and kimi work because `makeSession` fills them only when a scanner passes a `tasks` pair; null means "this store has no progress concept" and renders as an empty cell, while zcode's `(0, 0)` means "this session has no tasks yet".

Each scanner is tested against a temporary directory or database that mirrors the real on-disk layout — `QoderFx` for the jsonl plus task tree, a real node:sqlite `sessions` table plus lease JSON for hermes, the `session` and `todo` DDL for zcode, the `state.json` plus `wire.jsonl` tree for kimi code, and the two conversation maps for kimi work — with an injected `now` and no access to a real user store; these fixtures in `tests/scanners/fixtures.ts` are the executable statement of the layouts, so a store-format change must land as a scanner edit, a fixture edit and an update to the store reference page.

All five formats are snapshot-of-reality hazards rather than contracts: the schemas and value sets were observed on this machine at implementation and acceptance time (hermes end_reason seen only as NULL, cli_close, startup_orphan_reap and ws_orphan_reap; zcode todo status only as pending, in_progress and completed; all seven observed kimi work conversations completed), the fixtures encode the observation rather than a guarantee, and the code depends on none of that vocabulary beyond the null test, the literal "completed" and the `sess_subagent_` prefix, so most upstream renames surface as a skipped tool with one log line while a renamed qoder jsonl field degrades silently to IDLE.

Extending the integration to a new tool or store means one scanner plus a registry entry rather than a change to the unified model: a scanner with the `(root, now) => SessionInfo[]` signature returning `makeSession` records, registered in `SCANNERS` under the exact key used in the roots mapping, a root added to `defaultSessionRoots()`, and a fixture plus spec under `tests/scanners/` whose spec drives `collectSessions` with that root and a fixed `now`; the windows, failure isolation, age sort and record shape then apply for free, and for the row to be usable end to end the same key also needs a two-letter entry in the sessions card's `TOOL_TAGS` map (unknown keys render `??`) and a `config.json` `tools` entry whose absence degrades the click-through silently.

Both activity windows are applied inside each scanner rather than at the seam: every scanner drops rows whose age exceeds `ACTIVE_WINDOW = 600.0` on its own and decides liveness against `RUNNING_WINDOW = 90.0`, with the boundaries inclusive on the kept side (exactly 600 s is still listed, exactly 90 s is still RUN) and evaluated on the unrounded age before `makeSession` rounds it for display.

No JSON store is ever opened for writing: the qoder jsonl tail is read through `fs.openSync(file, 'r')` plus `readSync` on a binary handle, and every other JSON read in the module is `fs.readFileSync`, so the module contains no write path against any of the five stores and a scanner could not mutate a tool's data even by accident.

No store's body text ever reaches a session record: neither database's `title` column is selected (hermes projects `id, cwd, last_activity_at, started_at, end_reason, archived`; zcode projects `id, directory, time_updated, time_archived`), hermes' `ended_at` is likewise unused, the `todo` query aggregates counts without selecting `content`, and kimi code's `state.json` contributes only the `workDir` value out of its keys.

The qoder tail parser has no reporting error path: an unreadable file, a tail in which no line carries the `"type"` substring, and lines that fail to parse all collapse to `(null, null)`, which lands the session on IDLE with the directory-name project while the row stays in the list from its mtime — so drift inside the qoder jsonl format is the one store failure that produces neither a log line nor a missing tool.

The liveness signal a store can expose bounds the states its rows can ever carry: qoder is the only tool able to emit all four, because only its jsonl tail distinguishes an unanswered tool call; hermes emits RUN/DONE/IDLE, zcode and kimi code emit only RUN/DONE, and kimi work emits RUN/DONE/IDLE — so CONFIRM is unreachable for the four non-qoder tools and IDLE is unreachable for zcode and kimi code, the accepted distortion ADR-0003 records.
